newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Five Philippine state oil firm workers abducted.
newsitem.headline: Five Philippine state oil firm workers abducted.

text.p: A gang has abducted five workers of state-owned Philippine National Oil Co (PNOC) and demanded a five-million-peso ransom ($192,000) for their release, police said on Tuesday.

The five, were on their way to conduct geological surveys in Datu Odin Sinsuat town, Maguindanao province, 800 km (500 miles) south of Manila, when gunmen seized them, police general Roberto Lastimosa told reporters. He gave no other details.

Kidnappers last week abducted a Chinese trader in nearby Sultan Kudarat town and killed him when they were cornered by pursuing policemen. An ex-soldier has been arrested in connection with the trader's abduction.

Kidnapping for ransom has become a flourishing business in the Philippines with 241 people abducted last year. The gangs collected a total of $3.8 million in ransom, a citizens anti-crime watch group has said.
Relatives of victims generally refuse to report to the police because of widespread suspicion that soldiers and policemen are protecting the kidnappers.
